summary: preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload outside Node dependency graph
details: package.json declares a preinstall hook `node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (hex-named identifiers, inline decode maps) and downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<V>/<arch>.zip, then invokes the downloaded Bun binary via execFileSync against a sibling file `math_init.js`. math_init.js is a 727KB heavily obfuscated JavaScript file (string-array shift decoder using a `WV8StW` rotator, hex-mangled identifiers, thousands of literal codepoints). Executing an opaque, obfuscated payload with an alternate language runtime at install time is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: the payload runs outside the Node dependency graph and outside scanners that inspect only Node-resolved code. A React micro-frontend UI package has no build-time need for a separate Bun runtime to execute an obfuscated sibling script, and the rest of the tarball ships readable TypeScript build output, indicating the preinstall and math_init.js are foreign to the package's declared purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
